name: youtube/video-transcript-full
description: Fetch a YouTube video or Short transcript with timed segments and its provenance: whether the words are creator-written captions or machine speech recognition.

url.description: YouTube video or Short URL (e.g. "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ" or "https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Fir1x9cw2vg").

language.description: Preferred caption language code (e.g. "en", "es"). Defaults to English. If the video has no captions in that language, you get the transcript in another language the video has; the `language` field in the result says which. With `captionKind` set to "manual" or "automatic", no other language is returned.

captionKind.description: Which caption track to accept: "manual" only creator-written captions, "automatic" only YouTube's speech recognition, "any" whichever exists.

requireFields.description: Optional; omit it and routing is unchanged, with the cheapest source serving. Name the output fields this request must be able to return, for example `views`, and it is served only by a source that returns every one of them. Fields you do not name are still returned whenever the serving source has them. This can raise your price: when the cheapest source cannot return a named field, a dearer source serves, and you are quoted and charged its price. A named field can still be absent on a transcript that genuinely lacks it. Naming a combination that no single source returns together is refused as invalid input, with no charge.

pricing.note: Billed per call from metered usage; the reference price is typical.

readme:
# YouTube Video Transcript (Provenance) API

Returns the transcript of a YouTube video or Short as full text and as timed segments. It also says whether the captions were written by the creator or generated by speech recognition. It needs a YouTube video or Short URL.

## Use cases

- Index the spoken text of a video so you can search it by keyword.
- Pull timed lines from a video to build subtitles or jump links to exact moments.
- Check whether a video has creator-written captions before you rely on the text for quoting.
- Collect a video's transcript together with its title, channel and view count for content analysis.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/youtube/video-transcript-full" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | Yes | YouTube video or Short URL (e.g. "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ" or "https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Fir1x9cw2vg"). |
| `captionKind` | string | No | Which caption track to accept: "manual" only creator-written captions, "automatic" only YouTube's speech recognition, "any" whichever exists. |
| `language` | string | No | Preferred caption language code (e.g. "en", "es"). Defaults to English. If the video has no captions in that language, you get the transcript in another language the video has; the `language` field in the result says whi |
| `requireFields` | array | No | Optional; omit it and routing is unchanged, with the cheapest source serving. Name the output fields this request must be able to return, for example `views`, and it is served only by a source that returns every one of t |

## Example response

Real response for the request above, trimmed: lists keep their first item and long strings are cut.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "authorId": "UCuAXFkgsw1L7xaCfnd5JJOw",
    "authorUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCuAXFkgsw1L7xaCfnd5JJOw",
    "channel": "Rick Astley",
    "description": "The official video for “Never Gonna Give You Up” by Rick Astley. \n\nNever: The Au…",
    "durationSeconds": 213,
    "image": "https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dQw4w9WgXcQ/sddefault.jpg",
    "isAiGenerated": null,
    "isAutoGenerated": false,
    "keywords": [
      "rick astley"
    ],
    "language": "en",
    "segments": [
      {
        "endSeconds": 3.04,
        "startSeconds": 1.36,
        "text": "[♪♪♪]"
      }
    ],
    "title": "Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up (Official Video) (4K Remaster)"
  },
  "found": true
}
```

## Response fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `data.transcript` | The full transcript as one string. Segment texts are joined with spaces. |
| `data.segments[].text` | The text of one caption line. |
| `data.segments[].startSeconds / data.segments[].endSeconds` | Start and end time of the caption line, in seconds from the start of the video. |
| `data.isAutoGenerated` | `false` when the captions were written by the creator. Expect `true` for machine speech recognition. |
| `data.isAiGenerated` | Flag for AI-generated text. It is `null` in this response, so treat it as unknown. |
| `data.language` | Language code of the transcript returned. It can differ from the language you asked for. |
| `data.title / data.channel / data.durationSeconds` | Video title, channel name and video length in seconds. |
| `data.views` | View count of the video. |
| `data.authorId / data.authorUrl` | The channel ID and the channel URL of the video's author. |
| `data.videoId / data.url` | The video ID and the canonical watch URL. |

## Notes

- Set `captionKind` to `manual` or `automatic` to accept only that caption type. With either value, no other language is returned.
- If the video has no captions in the requested `language`, you get another language the video has. Check `data.language` to see which one.
- Name fields in `requireFields`, such as `views` or `likes`, when you need them present. This can route the call to a different source and change the price.
- If nothing is found, the call still succeeds and returns `found: false`. For more video metadata, call [YouTube Video Details](/apis/youtube/video-detail).

## Pricing

Billed at the actual cost of each call, about $0.002 for the request above. Failed calls are not charged.
